description: ThermGAS's own product line as published on thermgas.com (read 2026-11-07). Specs are vendor claims as written on each page; 'Not stated' means the page does not say. No prices are published.

families.name: Photoacoustic IR (PAIR) monitors
families.blurb: Selective, low-ppm, lamp-free; the technology behind the DMC and data center story.

families.name: CMOS refrigerant monitors
families.blurb: Lower-cost solid-state sensors for ASHRAE-style refrigerant leak notification.

families.name: Oxygen depletion
families.blurb: Electrochemical O2 monitoring for machinery rooms and storage.

families.name: Mechanical room safety equipment
families.blurb: Displays, calibration kits, switches, breathing apparatus and signage.

observations.text: The PAIR line (TracePoint 1000, Haloguard IR / III) is what the battery and data center stories rest on; CMOS and oxygen products are a separate, lower-cost refrigerant-safety line.
The Energy page claims explosion-proof enclosures certified for Class I, Div 1 and Div 2, but names no model, certifier or certificate, and no product page lists a hazardous-area rating.
Specs conflict inside ThermGAS pages: Haloguard III says 1 ppm in its header and 20 ppm in its spec table; the battery page and TracePoint say 0.5 ppm while Haloguard IR says 1 ppm.
Only TracePoint 1000 names data centers on its own product page; the Data Centers industry page names no model.
No product page publishes a price.
